newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Court backs Russian Rosgosstrakh selloff plans.
newsitem.headline: Court backs Russian Rosgosstrakh selloff plans.

text.p: A Moscow appeal court has ruled that the contested privatisation of Russian insurer Rosgosstrakh can continue while a lower court rules whether the privatisation is legal, a company spokeswoman said on Monday.
The lower court, which had suspended the privatisation pending a ruling on its legality, will consider the issue on Tuesday.
"The appeals court cancelled the court's decision to suspend privatisation of our company," OAO Rosgosstrakh spokeswoman Irina Aristova told Reuters.
A group of depositors at state savings bank Sberbank and Rosgosstrakh had brought suit and claimed privatisation was illegal while the company owed depositors huge sums of money.
Depositors said the privatisation scheme contained no provisions for payment.
Rosgosstrakh later filed an appeal to allow the process to continue.

The State Duma lower house of parliament estimates the debt at 30 billion roubles in 1992 prices (about $300 million at early 1992 exchange rate). Rosgosstrakh says its debt amounts to 24 billion roubles.

Under the privatisation scheme Rosgosstrakh employees bought 20 percent of shares, while its management team has a priority right to buy 30 percent. The remaining 50 percent will be offered for a cash auction later this year.
